current_leader.name: Cloud support-plan right-sizing engine
current_leader.state_transition: monthly cloud spend and provider-independent operational/incident telemetry update -> recompute current support-tier cost and required SLA/features -> compare cheaper eligible tiers -> recommend KEEP/DOWNGRADE/UPGRADE at next permissible boundary -> verify support-fee delta
current_leader.why_survived: AWS, Google Cloud and Azure all expose recurring paid support plans with explicit monthly pricing/change boundaries. Current searches still did not find an exact continuous cross-cloud engine combining support-tier economics with operational criticality/incident telemetry. The wedge remains read-only and the fee delta is deterministic.
current_leader.strongest_evidence: AWS paid support has a one-month minimum and explicit downgrade workflows; Google Cloud Standard/Enhanced/Premium have explicit minimum/percentage pricing; Azure support plans are billed monthly and can be changed/cancelled for eligible purchase channels. AWS Support API itself requires a paid plan, which constrains post-downgrade monitoring architecture.
current_leader.closest_threat: First-party calculators/change workflows, broad FinOps/MSP platforms, and partner-led support substitutes such as DoiT can absorb or economically neutralize the wedge. No exact continuous telemetry-aware optimizer was found.
current_leader.smallest_intervention: Read cloud billing forecast, current support tier, workload criticality/SLOs, incident history and required response-time/features from provider-independent telemetry; output KEEP/DOWNGRADE/UPGRADE plus next-month fee delta and feature/risk tradeoff; no automatic plan change.
current_leader.monetization: Small per-accepted plan-change fee, low recurring monitoring fee, or capped share of verified support-fee savings over a defined measurement window.
current_leader.biggest_unresolved_risk: The correct support tier may be mostly static and driven by tail-risk insurance rather than historical ticket usage; paid-plan-only support telemetry can disappear after downgrade, and most value may collapse into an annual review.
current_leader.next_research_test: Quantify real support-tier overprovisioning and change frequency; search MSP/FinOps products for explicit support-plan optimization; test whether provider-independent incident/SLO telemetry predicts tier sufficiency without paid Support APIs. Reject/demote if annual/static review captures most value or substitutes neutralize economics.

recent_cross_family_findings: Cloud support-plan right-sizing remains leader but was demoted from 48 to 46: low ticket usage cannot be treated as waste because support is tail-risk insurance; AWS Support API is paid-plan-only.
Support-plan economics generalize beyond AWS: Google Cloud has explicit monthly minimum/percentage tiers and Azure support is monthly/changeable for eligible channels.

App Store Small Business Program eligibility/requalification monitor survives at 45: Apple reduces commission to 15% for qualifying developers, but enrollment is simple and requalification is mostly annual, weakening monetization.
Unused prepaid shipping-label refund rejected: ShipStation Refund Assist now automatically detects, voids and submits eligible unused USPS labels for refund.
Commercial lease CAM overcharge recovery rejected: multiple exact products now automate lease-vs-statement audits and evidence-backed recovery/dispute workflows.
New rule: if a saving action removes access to the telemetry API used to recommend it, require provider-independent telemetry or penalize integration fragility.
New rule: do not infer support-tier waste from low support-case volume; model workload criticality, SLOs, response-time requirements and tail risk.
